question: UP-7 was negative, but two post-qualification confounds were found. What experiment should run next to isolate whether the transported state is directly readable?
evidence: UP-7 used a table-index-parity train/held-out split that accidentally withheld different entity-3 values between train and held-out data.
UP-7 used one linear head over state features plus an entity one-hot selector; that construction changes class biases but cannot make state-feature weights depend on the queried entity.
The scientific uncertainty is whether measurement loses useful phase/coherence information and whether depth/frame ambiguity remains after correcting those confounds.
constraints: Repair the identified split and query-conditioning confounds before adding new architectural machinery.
Keep transport unchanged and report scientific flags independently of harness acceptance.
Do not tune thresholds or budgets after seeing results.

candidates.proposal: Immediately add an explicit depth clock and inverse transport before repairing the UP-7 split and query-conditioning defects.
Keep the original magnitude-only observer and simply increase optimizer steps and hidden width.
Run a balanced combination split, use legitimate entity-conditioned heads, and compare magnitude-only versus phase/coherence-aware observation at fixed and unseen depths.
Lower the scientific success threshold until the original UP-7 observer qualifies.

expected_why: This directly repairs both identified confounds while isolating measurement loss from frame/depth ambiguity.
